The authors demonstrate RCS reduction of 20-25 dB with a prototype system
The RCS reduction is observed over a frequency range of 4-14 GHz
The plasma production technique used is seed-gas/UV photoionization
The maximum attenuation achieved for a 4-GHz EM wave transmitted through the plasma is 61 dB

The theoretical model developed for the plasma cloaking process includes scattering contributions from the plasma-vacuum interface, partial reflections from the plasma, and collisional absorption in the plasma
The plasma can be implemented as a 'shuttered' cloaking system, which can be switched on and off rapidly
The electron temperature required for the mean free path between collisions to be much smaller than the Debye length is very small
The condition for an EM wave to be totally reflected from an overdense plasma is the plasma density exceeding a critical value determined by the Lorentz equation
The expression for the dielectric constant of a collisionless plasma is ε = 1 - ωp^2 / ω^2
The authors develop a theoretical model for the plasma cloaking process
The model includes collisional absorption in the plasma
The plasma can be used to shield parts of existing vehicles having large radar cross sections
The plasma cloaking system can be used to provide protection against different radar threats
The authors demonstrate attenuation of up to 37 dB of reflected microwave signal from the plasma-filled enclosure
The RCS reduction achieved with the plasma-filled enclosure is from 20 to 25 dB over the frequency range of 4-14 GHz
